_comment: Every callsite under cli/** that can put a body on the wire, enumerated by bin/uplink-guard.py.
This is not a list of the uplinks somebody remembered: the guard lexes the code, finds every
body-capable callsite, and requires each one to be claimed by EXACTLY ONE row here — so an
undeclared send reddens CI, a row whose callsite is gone reddens it, and a row pointed at some
harmless line reddens it too. `callsite` is the code text of the line the row accounts for and
must be unique within its file. kind=json is an uplink (route + OpenAPI $ref + the wire test that
compares ITS body); kind=seam is a shared send implementation uplinks travel through; kind=skip is
reachable but out of scope, with the reason committed rather than left as a silent pass.
NOTE on codex-context / codex-tokens: one producer call (reportTokenUsage) emits both, so they
share a subtest. Their wire_needle values differ because each names a distinct line of that
subtest — both bodies ARE compared, the loop walks every captured request.

uplinks.seam_reason: ocagent's shared request builder: postJSON and every GET go through it. The method arrives as a variable, which is why the enumeration cannot key on a literal http.MethodPost.
The send half of the same shared builder above.

uplinks.skip_reason: Streams a raw body, not JSON — there is no request schema for a wire test to compare a body against. It is cmdUpload's own send: T-59 had extracted it into a shared postAttachment for `diff`, then `diff` stopped uploading at all (a comparison is a URL, not a stored blob) and the seam was folded back into its one caller.
The send half of the raw-bytes upload above.

uplinks.seam_reason: cmdDiff's ONE conditional hop: reached only when --external asks for the signed link, and the request it performs is ocagent-diff-share-link-mint below. The default flavour returns before this line without touching the network at all.

uplinks.skip_reason: GET with a nil body — nothing goes out. It asks GET /api/diff/share-link to mint the EXTERNAL comparison link, and it is the ONE request `diff` can make: only the server holds the signing key, so the default (internal) link is a pure local computation and this is what --external costs.
The send half of the bodyless mint GET above.

uplinks.seam_reason: Dispatch into cmdDiff. It sends NOTHING by default — the internal link is a pure function of the two addresses — and exactly one GET when --external asks the server to mint the signed one (ocagent-diff-share-link-mint below).

uplinks.skip_reason: GET with a nil body — nothing goes out.
The send half of the download above.

hop: the ONE place chat is drained since T-48 — both entrances (every connect and a chat delta) call l.drainChatNow(), which calls this. It is a GET (fetchChat), and since T-48 there IS a POST below it: the read receipt filed after the lines are printed. That POST is claimed by ocagent-chat-mark-read; this row stays a seam because the body is built there, not here.

uplinks.callsite: return newListener(cfg, env, out, once, stamper).run(rootCtx())
uplinks.seam_reason: hop: the process entry point. It builds the listener and enters run(), so every send this subcommand ever makes hangs below this one line — all of them already claimed on their own callsites (ocagent-run-1..9, ocagent-connectonce, ocagent-dispatch-value, ocagent-chat-mark-read). This line itself puts nothing on the wire. It is NEW as a callsite only because T-89 split the construction out of cmdListen into newListener so the wiring could be asserted; before that the same hop was spelled `return l.run(ctx)`, which the scan did not match. Nothing about what goes on the wire changed.
builds the wind-down hook. It no longer closes over any send: the hook wakes the session with the notice the server pushed and leaves the stop reports to the session's own MCP calls.
builds the recycle hook; the sends it closes over are declared on their own callsites

hop to the codex identity POST declared by codex-identity. The anchor deliberately runs to the CLOSING argument of handleListenerLine rather than stopping at requestRateLimits: independent review swapped that third argument for a no-op `func(string) {}` and every codex member went permanently silent — no notice, no chat event, no task event ever became a turn — with all three Go suites AND this guard green. Deleting the whole call was already caught here by accident (the reportIdentity/requestRateLimits pair lives in the closure); replacing one argument was caught by nothing. Pinning `s.openListenerTurn)` inside the anchor is what makes that swap red.

the dispatch handler handed over as a VALUE: the stream calls it for every frame, and the sends below it are the frame handlers' own (member refetch, chat/reply-card/task drains). Taking the value is the callsite here — the call itself is spelled onData(…) inside the stream loop, a name no rule can know. It used to name the presence POST as what hangs below; that retired with the client-side stop reports (T-a9d6).

the host seam constructor handed over as a VALUE (the package variable every entry point resolves through). The requests it reaches — the ocagent download GET and the probes — are claimed on their own callsites.
the command-frame handler handed to the SSE scanner as a VALUE: the loop calls it per frame and it reaches the command_result receipts, each declared on its own callsite in command.go.

uplinks.skip_reason: The credential-renewal POST, and it carries NO body at all (the third argument is a literal nil). The endpoint names no target on purpose — the machine acted on is the caller's verified sub — so there is nothing for a wire test to compare against a request schema, and the frozen spec declares no requestBody for the operation.
The send half of the body-less renewal POST above.

uplinks.read_reason: Presents a CANDIDATE credential at the cheapest read-only endpoint a warden is entitled to, before anything on disk is replaced. A GET through the shared getter: no body goes out, and the frozen spec is checked to declare no requestBody for it.

uplinks.skip_reason: Invocation of the body-less renewal POST (warden-renew-request). No body is built here or anywhere below it.
